title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Cadmium (Cd, Z=48) is 112.414(4)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Cadmium (Cd, Z=48) as 112.414(4), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 48, symbol Cd, as Cadmium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Cadmium as 112.414(4). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Geological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material. The difference between the atomic weight of the element in such materials and that given in the table may exceed the stated uncertainty. Isotope rows in the same file: Cd-106 relative atomic mass 105.9064599(12), isotopic composition 0.0125(6); Cd-108 relative atomic mass 107.9041834(12), isotopic composition 0.0089(3); Cd-110 relative atomic mass 109.90300661(61), isotopic composition 0.1249(18); Cd-111 relative atomic mass 110.90418287(61), isotopic composition 0.1280(12); Cd-112 relative atomic mass 111.90276287(60), isotopic composition 0.2413(21); Cd-113 relative atomic mass 112.90440813(45), isotopic composition 0.1222(12); Cd-114 relative atomic mass 113.90336509(43), isotopic composition 0.2873(42); Cd-116 relative atomic mass 115.90476315(17), isotopic composition 0.0749(18). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
